model.area_formula: A_engine = A_fixed + NC * A_column; sharing fixed service between engines not credited
omitted_area: router and output identity scatter delta
new rank activation fanout beyond inherited service
model.arithmetic: Eight 32-term blockdot lanes and 64 BF16 lanes per column; one format active at a time. Lane feedback slots are included in arithmetic proxy, not a second additive area.
model.clocks: 1.2GHz used only for bandwidth sizing, not new SS/FF qualification

schedule.exact_expert_formula: For each expert e, pass_count_e=ceil(number_of_live_verify_positions_selecting_e/NC). Sum over e when positions can be compacted per expert. Fixed position waves use sum_w |union experts in wave w| and can be larger.
schedule.union_statistics_limitation: Current artifact has union means and mean maximum multiplicity only, not full per-expert occupancy histogram or actual draft IDs. Fixed-wave mean is a trace-informed sensitivity; not worst-case and not guaranteed for drafts.
schedule.downstream: GU can concatenate expert output rows only with identical activation per position and exact per-row rounding. Down has distinct expert intermediates per position and needs independent operand identities; do not merge reductions.
schedule.selection: Process all six verify positions. Accepted prefix masks mutable-state commit only; tau3.8879 does not scale verification arithmetic.
schedule.activation_compaction: Fixed position waves require NC resident activation columns. Arbitrary per-expert position compaction requires all six positions resident or explicitly priced context reload/operand gather; extra SRAM figures retain inherited bank organization and omit mux/port logic.
schedule.source: NC increases reuse per weight record, not record rate. More row engines require proportionally more ROM ports/bank selection, activation fanout and output bandwidth; the lower-bound area sweep does not prove their availability.
schedule.exactness: Position/expert/layer tags and validity masks; preserve every 32-term scaled block and chunk8 golden reduction; padding inactive columns cannot alter active reductions. No associative reordering.
schedule.draft: Five positions for three DSpark stages plus LM head, followed by five SERIAL Markov steps. Wide columns help only parallel matrix stages; serial draft dependencies remain.

conclusions: Uniform NC1 sacrifices dense P6 parallelism. Equal compute area buys only A6/A1 more row engines, substantially less than six.
For routed experts, shared weights occur only on intersection of selected IDs; six columns can be mostly idle. Repeated-six and disjoint36 extremes must both be screened.

Candidate architecture is heterogeneous pools or dynamically reassigned matrix workgroups: wide column pools for common-weight dense/shared/draft/head, narrow row-parallel pools for sparse expert masks. This is an analytical direction, not an implementation decision.
AR and P6 schedules must both include full service, activation delivery, mutable attention, gather/scatter and collectives. No whole-model microsecond prediction follows from these ratios.
More engines across128ranks only confer ideal work distribution benefits if native rank ownership/collective trees are preserved or explicitly re-priced. Small matrices may not occupy all engines.
